official_sources: HMLR PG40 supplement 4 boundary agreements/determined boundaries
HM Land Registry Customer Care Review 2025
official_measurement_examples: most registered title boundaries follow the general-boundaries rule
red edging shows general position rather than the exact legal boundary
a determined boundary records an exact line when sufficient evidence is provided
boundary agreement and determined-boundary procedures are distinct
HMLR does not resolve the underlying neighbour dispute merely by recording a determined line
Ordnance Survey base mapping is not a cadastral guarantee of legal extent
title-plan boundary evidence does not establish planning permission infrastructure capacity or final development yield
core_rules: general boundary is not exact legal line
red edging is not survey-grade cadastral geometry
determined boundary is distinct from general boundary
boundary agreement is distinct from determined boundary
OS feature is not automatic legal boundary
title plan scale must be retained
plan update is not ownership transfer
boundary application is not planning permission
planning permission does not determine title boundary
boundary dispute requires evidence beyond map overlay
title plan may refer to general extent only
index-map search is not title proof by itself
boundary status does not prove access rights
boundary status does not calculate yield
no parcel boundary clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official HM Land Registry, GOV.UK and Land Registration legislation checked 2026-07-26. PG40 supplement 4 update dated 1 June 2026 retained; no parcel promotion.
